_note: Curated news-anchor banks (natural AMERICAN English, one learning point per entry). gen_news.py turns each entry into a lesson spec; beats alternate Ama/Carlos. three: [phrase, reply]x3 | fix: bad, good, ex1, ex2, rule | ab: A, B, ask, answer, example | ways: polite, neutral, casual, tip1, tip2 | pov: situation, answer, alt answer, avoid, why. Card fields: [text, sub] (cards >= 52 px, checked).

items.point: hotel requests: late checkout, Wi-Fi, towels
beats: Could I get a late checkout?
Could I get a late checkout?
The Wi-Fi isn't working in my room.
Sorry about that. I'll reset it.
Could I get some extra towels?
Of course. I'll send some up.
rows: Could I get a late checkout?

items.point: ordering coffee: can I get, to go, pay by card
beats: Can I get a medium latte, please?
Can I get a medium latte?
Could I get that to go?
Could I get that to go?
to go = take it with you
rows: Can I get a medium latte?
Could I get that to go?

items.point: pharmacy phrases: something for, prescription, how often
beats: I need something for a headache.
Do I need a prescription for this?
No, you can buy it here.
How often should I take it?
How often should I take it?
rows: I need something for a headache.
How often should I take it?

items.point: subway directions: which line, transfer, how many stops
on the plane: could I get, mind switching seats, overhead bin
beats: Could I get some water, please?
Is there room in the overhead bin?
rows: Is there room in the overhead bin?

items.point: bank phrases: open an account, withdraw cash, fee
beats: I'd like to open a checking account.
I'd like to open an account.
Can I withdraw some cash here?
Is there a fee for that?
Is there a fee for that?
rows: I'd like to open an account.
Is there a fee for that?

items.point: IELTS Speaking: phrases to buy time and extend answers
beats: To be honest, I prefer the city.
For example, there's more to do.

items.point: agree is a verb: I agree, not I am agree
beats: A lot of learners say: I am agree.
agree is a verb, no am

items.point: discuss + object, no about
beats: People often say: let's discuss about the plan.
We need to discuss the budget.
But you can talk about the budget.

items.point: questions with does: how much does it cost
beats: Many learners ask: how much it cost?
Say: how much does it cost?
How much do these apples cost?
Or just say: how much is it?
Does for it, do for they.

items.point: say vs tell: she told me, not she said me
beats: People often say: she said me the news.
Say: she told me the news.
She said that it was late.
He told me to wait here.

items.point: look for: I'm looking for a book
beats: Many people say: I'm looking a book.
Say: I'm looking for a book.
Can I help you find something?
Can I help you find it?
Yes, I'm looking for a cookbook.
Look at it, look for it.

items.point: L1 mistake: I really like it, not I very like it
beats: A lot of learners say: I very like it.
very can't go before a verb
Or: I like it a lot.
Very goes with adjectives: very good.
Really before verbs, very before adjectives.

items.point: do yoga, not make yoga
beats: Option A: I do yoga every morning.
Option B: I make yoga every morning.
Which one is right? Comment below.
It's A. I do yoga every morning.
You also do homework and do the dishes.

items.point: make dinner, not do dinner
beats: Option A: I'll do dinner tonight.
Option B: I'll make dinner tonight.
Which one sounds natural? Comment below.
It's B. I'll make dinner tonight.
You also make coffee and make a cake.

items.point: phrasal verb + pronoun: try it on
beats: Option A: Can I try on it?
Option B: Can I try it on?
Which one is right? Comment below.
It's B. Can I try it on?
Can I try on this jacket? Also fine.

items.point: borrow vs lend
beats: Option A: Can I borrow your pen?
Option B: Can I lend your pen?
Which one is right? Comment below.
It's A. Can I borrow your pen?
Or ask: can you lend me your pen?
Can you lend me your pen?
rows: Can you lend me your pen?

items.point: get in a taxi, get on a bus
beats: Option A: I got in the taxi.
Option B: I got on the taxi.
Which one is right? Comment below.
It's A. I got in the taxi.
But you get on a bus or a train.
get on a bus / a train
rows: get in a taxi / a car
get on a bus / a train

items.point: in the morning, on Monday
beats: Option A: I run in the morning.
Option B: I run on the morning.
Which one is right? Comment below.
It's A. I run in the morning.
But we say on Monday morning.

items.point: booking a doctor's appointment: polite to casual
beats: Polite: I'd like an appointment, please.
Neutral: Can I book a visit?
Casual: Can I see a doctor today?
Can I see a doctor today?
On the phone, the first one is best.
The others are fine in person too.
rows: I'd like to make an appointment.
Can I see a doctor today?

items.point: saying no to an invitation: polite to casual
beats: Polite: I'd love to, but I can't.
I'd love to, but I can't.
Neutral: Sorry, I can't make it.
Casual: Can't tonight. Maybe next time!
Use the first one with your boss.
Save the casual one for friends.
rows: I'd love to, but I can't.

items.point: disagreeing politely at work
beats: Polite: I see your point, but I'm not sure.
Neutral: I'm not sure about that.
Casual: Hmm, I don't think so.
In meetings, start with the first one.
With close coworkers, the others are fine.

items.point: asking for help: polite to casual
beats: Polite: Would you mind helping me out?
Neutral: Could you help me, please?
Casual: Can you give me a hand?
Can you give me a hand?
With strangers, use the first two.
Give me a hand is great with friends.
give me a hand = help me
rows: Can you give me a hand?

items.point: ordering food politely: I'll have
beats: You're at a restaurant. The server asks: ready to order?
Say: I'll have the salmon, please.
Or: Could I get the pasta, please?
I want can sound a little rude here.

items.point: sending a package: I'd like to send
beats: You're at the post office with a package. What do you say?
Say: I'd like to send this to Canada.
Then ask: how long will it take?
Don't say: I want send this.
Want needs to before a verb.
rows: I'd like to send this to Canada.

items.point: asking for a table: could we sit
beats: You want a table outside. What do you say?
Say: Could we sit outside, please?
Or: Do you have a table by the window?
Don't say: Give us table outside.
That sounds like an order, not a request.

items.point: asking for another size: do you have this in
beats: The shirt is too small. What do you ask?
Say: Do you have this in a large?
Do you have this in a large?
Or: Do you have it in blue?
Do you have it in blue?
Start with do you have. It sounds polite.
rows: Do you have this in a large?
Do you have it in blue?
